title: Leaders Who Trapped Their People
overview: God, speaking through the prophet Hosea, charges the leaders of Israel and Judah with leading the people away from him, warns of coming war, and says that turning to the empire of Assyria for help will not heal them.

parts.label: Leaders put on trial (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: Priests, people and the royal family are all called to account, because the leaders have been like hunters' traps set at Mizpah and Tabor, places that may have had worship sites. Hosea pictures Israel's worship of other gods as sexual unfaithfulness to the LORD, and God says none of it is hidden from him.

parts.label: Too far gone to return (vv. 4-7)
parts.note: Their habits have such a grip that they no longer even know God, and their pride testifies against them; Judah, the southern kingdom, is now stumbling too. Bringing animals to sacrifice will not reach a God who has withdrawn, and even their monthly New Moon feasts will come with ruin to their land.

parts.label: Alarm on the border (vv. 8-9)
parts.note: Trumpets sound in Gibeah, Ramah and Beth Aven, towns in Benjamin's territory on the border between north and south, as an enemy closes in. Many scholars link this to the war between Israel and Judah around 735 BC, though the exact setting is uncertain.

parts.label: Moving the boundary stones (vv. 10-12)
parts.note: Moving the stones that marked a family's land was a form of theft the law forbade, so Judah's leaders are accused of grabbing what is not theirs. God pictures himself as a moth and as rot, slowly eating away at both kingdoms from the inside.

parts.label: The wrong doctor (vv. 13-15)
parts.note: Seeing their sickness, the northern kingdom (often called Ephraim) and Judah ran to the king of Assyria for help, as their kings did historically, but he could not heal them, and the Hebrew title used for him here is unclear. God says he will act like a lion and then withdraw to his den until, in their misery, they admit their guilt and truly seek him.

think: When something in your life or community is clearly going wrong, what makes it tempting to look for an outside fix rather than face the cause?
